results.note: The migration does bound the result with `limit greatest(coalesce(p_point_limit,0),0)`. But the only test that runs the real RPC is marked @pytest.mark.integration, and pyproject.toml:33 (`-m 'not integration'`) deselects it. The new offline test (line 80) calls `_contract_rows`, a Python copy of the SQL logic at lines 22-41. It asserts against that copy, not the function, so it proves nothing about the RPC.

The SQL orders by source_timestamp desc, id desc and filters on status in ('OK','STALE') and source_timestamp not null. The DB test is integration-marked and was deselected. The offline tests at :108 (Python simulation) and :163 (SQL string match) do not execute the function.

The RPC takes a required p_source_vendor filter. The DB test that proves a call returns one vendor is integration-marked and was deselected. The offline test at :129 filters a Python list with `_contract_rows`, which is tautological.

`coalesce(jsonb_agg(...), '[]'::jsonb)` should return []. The DB test is integration-marked and was not run. The offline test at :151 passes an empty list into the Python simulation and asserts []. That is trivially true and says nothing about the SQL, and no web test covers the empty state.

The live PostgREST test is integration-marked and no gate ran it. Nothing shows the migration was applied to the live Supabase project, so the assumption research flagged (one JSON array under the PostgREST row cap) is still unverified.

`uv run pytest -q` exited 0 (344 passed, 71 deselected), and the web test and typecheck gates also exited 0. The suite partly stays green because DB-backed tests are excluded, and this diff excluded one more (see note).
